advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the timeout-marker scan read the `timeout=` keyword and bare `mark.timeout`, and fail on any timeout marker whose value it cannot read
evidence: tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py:118-121: requires `isinstance(node.func.value, ast.Attribute)` and `node.args and isinstance(node.args[0], ast.Constant)`, so keyword-only calls and a bare `mark` Name are dropped
tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py:140-144: the self-test treats `@pytest.mark.timeout(seconds=9)` as expected-skipped, which shows keyword calls are dropped on purpose without any report
pytest-timeout accepts the timeout as a `timeout=` keyword on the marker, so `@pytest.mark.timeout(timeout=3)` is a valid way to set a tight budget
advisory.finding: The scan skips the keyword form `pytest.mark.timeout(timeout=N)` and markers written as bare `mark.timeout(N)` without reporting anything, so a too-tight marker in either form escapes the floor check.
scenarios: A new test written as `@pytest.mark.timeout(timeout=3)` or with `from pytest import mark` and `@mark.timeout(3)` passes the scan and crashes workers on loaded hosts.
advisory.suggested_fix: Also accept `ast.Name` with id 'mark' as the receiver. Read the value from `node.args[0]` or the `timeout` keyword. Collect timeout calls whose value is not a literal and fail on them instead of skipping them.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the real-tree scan found at least the known review-bot markers before trusting an empty offender list
evidence: tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py:154-159: offenders built from `(root / "tests").rglob("*.py")` with no assertion that any file or marker was found
tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py:161: `assert not offenders` is the only assertion
The removed test asserted `seconds is not None` for a known marker; the replacement drops that check that the scan ran
advisory.finding: The real-tree scan has no check that it found any markers, so if the root or glob is wrong (empty list) the test passes vacuously and looks the same as a clean tree.
scenarios: A refactor moves the module or changes parents[2], so rglob yields nothing and the guard keeps passing while checking nothing.
advisory.suggested_fix: Gather every (path, line, seconds) found, then assert the list is non-empty and includes tests/unit/test_review_bot.py before checking for offenders.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make _timeout_marker_values also read a literal `timeout=` keyword argument, and change the fixture case from `seconds=9` to `timeout=9` with the expected list updated to include it
evidence: tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py:120: `and node.args` — only a positional first argument is ever inspected; keywords are never read
tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py:140: `"@pytest.mark.timeout(seconds=9)\n"` — the fixture's keyword case uses a parameter name pytest-timeout does not have
tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py:144: `assert _timeout_marker_values(source) == [(2, 4), (4, 2.5)]` — this asserts keyword markers are dropped
pytest-timeout's marker signature is `timeout(timeout=..., method=..., func_only=...)`, so `timeout=3` is a valid way to set the budget
advisory.finding: The census skips the keyword form `@pytest.mark.timeout(timeout=3)`, which pytest-timeout accepts. A too-tight marker written that way gets past the guard. The fixture test hides this: it asserts that `timeout(seconds=9)` is skipped, but `seconds` is not a real pytest-timeout parameter, so the skip is never tested against a real keyword shape.
scenarios: A contributor writes `@pytest.mark.timeout(timeout=3)` on a new test. The census returns no offenders, the marker covers the autouse git probes in setup and teardown, and the worker crashes on a loaded host. That is exactly the bug this change fixes.
advisory.suggested_fix: When there are no positional args, also look for `kw.arg == "timeout"` with an `ast.Constant` value in `node.keywords`. In the fixture, replace `seconds=9` with `timeout=9` and expect `(8, 9)` in the result.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Before checking for offenders, assert the census found a non-empty set of markers, including the known test_review_bot.py webhook markers
evidence: tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py:156: `for path in sorted((root / "tests").rglob("*.py"))` — an empty iteration is never detected
tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py:161: `assert not offenders, (` — the only assertion is that something is absent
The removed test asserted `seconds is not None` before `seconds >= 30`. That presence check confirmed the marker was actually found, and the replacement has nothing equivalent.
tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:1800: `@pytest.mark.timeout(30)` — a known marker the census could be required to find
advisory.finding: The whole-tree census only asserts `not offenders` and never checks that the scan found anything. If the root path resolves wrong, `rglob` returns nothing, or the matcher stops recognizing the tree's real marker syntax, the test still passes. A pass cannot be told apart from a scan that saw nothing.
scenarios: A move or rename changes `parents[2]` or the tests/ layout, the scan reads zero files, and the guard stays green while too-tight markers are added.
advisory.suggested_fix: Collect every `(path, line, seconds)` found into a list, then `assert any(str(p).endswith("tests/unit/test_review_bot.py") for p, _, _ in found)` (or `assert found`) before filtering for offenders.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Require timeout markers to be strictly above the git-probe worst case (plus body headroom), not just equal to it
evidence: test_review_bot.py diff: '@pytest.mark.timeout(30)' with comment 'so it must clear their bound, not just the body'
tests/conftest.py:789-793: setup and teardown each call _repo_head, each up to 3 x 5 s
dropped.finding: The floor accepts a marker exactly equal to the worst-case autouse git probe time (30 s), so the 30 s markers this change adds leave no time for the test body or other autouse fixtures when the probes run long.
scenarios: Loaded host: the setup rev-parse succeeds on its third attempt at about 14.9 s and teardown takes a similar time. The 30 s thread timeout then fires partway through and kills the xdist worker, which is the failure this change is meant to prevent.
dropped.suggested_fix: Use `<=` (or add an explicit body-headroom term to the floor) and raise the 30 s markers above the new floor.
